action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
The current board state has pieces only in column 3, with an x at the bottom (row 5) and an o directly above it (row 4). All columns are playable since none are full at the top (row 0). No immediate threats or wins exist for either player, as each has only one piece and the win condition requires four in a row.

The center column (3) is the most critical area on the board. If x plays anywhere else, o can respond by playing in column 3 (placing an o at row 3). This would create two consecutive o's vertically in the center (at rows 4 and 3), giving o a strong positional advantage to build upon horizontally, vertically, or diagonally in subsequent turns.

By contrast, playing in column 3 places an x at row 3. This produces an x-o-x stack in the center column. It directly occupies the key spot o would otherwise claim, preventing o from forming consecutive pieces there. The resulting alternating pattern (if o later responds in the same column) neutralizes the column for both players. The newly placed x also occupies a highly central square (row 3, column 3), which supports strong future connections in multiple directions: horizontal lines at row 3, diagonals extending from it, and potential follow-up moves in the same column if o ignores it (e.g., allowing x to later create consecutive x's higher up).

This move maintains central control without allowing o an easy advantage, consistent with optimal early-game strategy in Connect 4 (prioritizing the center while countering the opponent's piece there). Side columns (e.g., 2 or 4) would connect x's existing piece horizontally but would leave the critical center spot open for o to exploit.

Final Answer: 3

Column 3 is the most central column and therefore the highest-value column on the board. Placing in column 3 lands an X on row 1, producing the vertical sequence X-O-X-O-X from the bottom. This move accomplishes three important things at once:

- X now leads 3-2 in total pieces.
- The new X occupies the only remaining square that O could have used to connect its own two O's into a vertical pair (row 1-2). After the move, O's pieces remain isolated.
- Although the alternating pattern prevents a vertical win inside column 3, the three X's still participate in many horizontal and diagonal lines that can be developed in the largely empty board.

That reply would equalize the piece count (3-3) and simultaneously give O two vertically adjacent pieces, handing O the initiative. Because the board is otherwise empty, the first player to seize the center column keeps the long-term advantage.

No immediate win exists for either player, and no forcing threat can be created in a single ply. The move in column 3 therefore maximizes piece count, central control, and prevention of O's connectivity, which is the optimal choice under perfect play.
